skill.name: langgraph
skill.description: Guides users through LangGraph agent architecture, including graph construction, state reducers, conditional routing, tool nodes, persistence patterns, and production anti-patterns.
skill.summary: Build stateful LangGraph agent workflows with clear graph structure, routing, and state management.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The only confirmed issue is an unsafe LangGraph calculator example that exposes eval() on tool input. The remaining backtick findings are markdown formatting false positives, and no prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: Unsafe eval() in calculator tool example
remediation.suggestion: Replace eval() with a safe math parser, allowlisted operators, or a trusted calculator library before publishing the example.

remediation.issue: Missing safety warning for tool input execution
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance that agent tools must validate inputs and must not execute arbitrary model-provided expressions.

content.value_statement: Stateful agent systems can become hard to trace and maintain. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code design clearer LangGraph workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains StateGraph construction with nodes, edges, START, and END.
Shows how reducers manage shared state updates across nodes.
Demonstrates conditional routing for multi-path agent workflows.
Covers tool node integration for ReAct-style agent loops.
Highlights production concerns such as persistence, human review, and loop exits.
limitations: Examples focus on Python LangGraph usage.
It does not install LangGraph or configure API credentials.
The calculator example needs replacement before production use.
It provides patterns, not a complete deployed agent service.

use_cases.title: Prototype a ReAct Agent
use_cases.description: Create a small LangGraph agent that routes between an LLM node and tool execution.

use_cases.title: Plan Shared Agent State
use_cases.description: Design state fields and reducers for teams of agents that update shared workflow data.

use_cases.title: Review Agent Workflow Design
use_cases.description: Check graph routing, exit conditions, and state boundaries before building a production workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Graph
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a single agent workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a simple LangGraph workflow with one agent node, one tool node, and a clear END condition.

prompt_templates.title: Design State Reducers
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate state planning for multiple nodes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my agent state fields and recommend reducers for messages, findings, sources, and current workflow step.

prompt_templates.title: Add Conditional Routing
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create conditional routing for coding, search, and chat paths based on a classifier node.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate my LangGraph design for persistence, loop exits, human review points, tool safety, and debugging gaps.

output_examples.input: I need a LangGraph agent that can call tools and stop when no tool call is needed.
output_examples.output: A recommended graph layout with an agent node, a tool node, conditional routing, and an END path.

output_examples.input: My workflow has researchers and writers updating the same state.
output_examples.output: A state design that separates accumulated findings, source lists, messages, and current step tracking.

output_examples.input: I want to prevent my agent from looping forever.
output_examples.output: A review checklist covering max iterations, task completion flags, timeout limits, and clear terminal routes.

best_practices: Define state fields before adding nodes or routing logic.
Use reducers only for fields that should accumulate or merge.
Add explicit END conditions, iteration limits, and persistence plans.
anti_patterns: Do not use unsafe dynamic evaluation inside agent tools.
Do not build loops without clear exit conditions.
Do not place unrelated workflow data in one large state object.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps design LangGraph workflows for stateful agents, tool calling, routing, and shared state management.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is this a complete LangGraph application?
faq.answer: No. It is guidance and example structure for building your own LangGraph application.

faq.question: What should I change before production use?
faq.answer: Replace unsafe dynamic evaluation, validate all tool inputs, and add persistence, timeouts, and review checkpoints.

faq.question: Who is this skill best for?
faq.answer: It is best for developers and technical leads building agent workflows with LangGraph and LangChain.

faq.question: Does it explain common mistakes?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers infinite loops, stateless nodes, and overly large state objects.
